video_title: Josh Donaldson on Michael Jordan's Mentality, MLB Trash Talk + Playing With a CHIP on His Shoulder

quotes.speaker: Josh Donaldson
quotes.summary_phrase: Josh Donaldson on his intense, competitive mindset during his youth
quotes.excerpt: I had such a will to want to beat whoever was in front of me
quotes.quote: I think from when I was younger, I always played intense. I had such a will to want to beat whoever was in front of me that I didn't care. Whatever it took, I was going to do. When you're working out, I was that guy that was doing, everybody's going to do 20, now I'm going to do 40. It just didn't matter. I was going to make sure that I was in better shape than everybody. There wasn't anybody that was going to outwork me.
quotes.social_post: Josh Donaldson reflects on his intense competitive nature as a young athlete saying he always had a will to beat whoever was in front of him and he was going to make sure nobody outworked him.

quotes.speaker: Josh Donaldson
quotes.summary_phrase: Josh Donaldson on his relentless training routine as a young athlete
quotes.excerpt: I would sit there and go in and hit 500 balls right-handed, 500 balls left-handed
quotes.quote: During the summer when I was playing baseball, I had configured this net in my backyard. It was probably eight foot tall, probably five feet wide. I would sit there and go in and hit 500 balls right-handed, 500 balls left-handed. I'd go in the pool, I was doing laps in the pool. I was doing sit-ups because you hear Herschel Walker, those guys, they were doing 1,000 sit-ups a day and push-ups. I was doing all of that. And I'd go inside and I'd tell my mom, I just did 500 swings left-handed and right-handed. She's like, that's good. She's like, I bet there was somebody that did 501. I just wasn't satisfied with doing enough.
quotes.social_post: Josh Donaldson details his relentless training routine as a young athlete including hitting 1000 balls a day and doing hundreds of sit ups to ensure he was never satisfied with just doing enough.

quotes.speaker: Josh Donaldson
quotes.summary_phrase: Josh Donaldson on his insecurity and need to win
quotes.excerpt: I never felt like what I had was enough and I felt like I needed more to get that
quotes.quote: I never felt like what I had was enough and I felt like I needed more to get that. And it came across that way because I played with a certain intensity because I wanted to win. I always loved the Michael Jordan 'The Last Dance' documentary. Somebody said I took that personal. Before that was a thing, I was doing that. I tried to find something about the opposition and I made it very easy for them also to find something about me.
quotes.social_post: Josh Donaldson says he was taking things personal long before Michael Jordan made it famous in The Last Dance. He explains how he used his insecurity and need to win to fuel his intensity on the field.

quotes.speaker: Josh Donaldson
quotes.summary_phrase: Josh Donaldson on avoiding complacency in a long baseball season
quotes.excerpt: When you play as many games in baseball as you do, it gets monotonous
quotes.quote: When you play as many games in baseball as you do, it gets monotonous. It's very easy just to go into this almost like coma. You go through the motions is what we would call it. For me to stay away from that, I had to find something. I tried to find something about the opposition and I made it very easy for them also to find something about me.
quotes.social_post: Josh Donaldson discusses the challenge of avoiding complacency during a long baseball season and how he used trash talk to keep himself engaged and motivated against the opposition.

quotes.speaker: Josh Donaldson
quotes.summary_phrase: Josh Donaldson on the ability to flip a switch before games
quotes.excerpt: They say that you can't flip a switch, but I had a switch for sure
quotes.quote: Before the game, it was just you're trying to, they say that you can't flip a switch, but I had a switch for sure. Especially early in my career, I could get away with it more than in the end because everybody kind of knew me at the end of my career. They knew that I was a fun guy. We're over here razing each other, we're talking crap to each other. Early on, it was easy for me to be that fun-loving teammate, camaraderie guy, and then once the game showed up, switch. I don't care who is out there. I'm here to let you know that I'm here and I'm winning.
quotes.social_post: Josh Donaldson pushes back on the idea that you cannot flip a switch before a game. He says he definitely had a switch early in his career that allowed him to go from a fun teammate to a fierce competitor once the game started.

quotes.speaker: Josh Donaldson
quotes.summary_phrase: Josh Donaldson on Johnny Gomes' mentorship and perspective
quotes.excerpt: Johnny Gomes was one of my teammates and he was somewhat of a mentor to me
quotes.quote: The last time I got recalled, Johnny Gomes was one of my teammates and he was somewhat of a mentor to me. I don't know if he was trying to be, but I kind of gravitated towards him a little bit. I remember I'd hit a home run or something like that and I was like, dude, did I pimp that too hard? I don't want to piss anybody off. He looked me in the eye and he said, you know how hard you worked to hit a home run in the big leagues? I said, yeah, actually I do. And he's like, it's okay for you to enjoy it. If you go excessive on it, I'll let you know.
quotes.social_post: Josh Donaldson shares a lesson from former teammate Johnny Gomes about enjoying success in the big leagues. Gomes told him you know how hard you worked to hit a home run so it is okay to enjoy it.
